scripts.radio: Habari zenu, listeners. This is Kenya on Record. Today, we address what happens when a mother returns to work after maternity leave. For far too long, working mothers in this country have been forced into degrading compromises—expressing milk in dirty office washrooms, enduring subtle penalties from HR, or being pushed out of their jobs entirely. That era is officially closing. Under the newly enacted legal provisions, every employer is now mandated to provide a clean, private, and sanitary breastfeeding space, alongside designated nursing breaks during working hours. Let us be clear: this is not a corporate perk. It is not an act of benevolence from your CEO. It is a statutory obligation under our labour laws. It exists to safeguard child health and ensure that a woman's career does not come at the cost of basic human dignity. If your workplace employs staff, setting up a safe, hygienic lactation space is now as mandatory as having clean running water or an occupational health standard. To every working mother listening today: understand your rights, cite the law, and refuse to let anyone treat your child’s nourishment as an inconvenience. Kwa kifupi: Sheria mpya sasa inalazimisha waajiri wote kutoa nafasi safi na salama za kunyonyesha, pamoja na kutoa muda rasmi wa kina mama kunyonyesha wakiwa kazini. Hii si hisani ya ofisi; ni haki yako kisheria.
scripts.voice_note: Morning team, quick update from Kenya on Record that you need to pass around. If you or someone you know has recently returned to work after maternity leave, take note. The law now formally requires employers to provide clean, private, and secure lactation spaces, along with dedicated daily breaks for working mothers to express milk. The days of mothers pumping in cramped, unsanitary office toilets or feeling intimidated by management are over. An employer cannot legally dock your pay or penalize you for utilizing these breaks. It is a standard workplace requirement, plain and simple. If your HR department is pretending not to know the update, hold them accountable. Pass this note to any working mother or office group that needs to hear it today.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Employers are now legally required to give mothers clean breastfeeding rooms and daily breaks. Do not let HR treat your legal rights as a favor.
scripts.reels: Pumping breastmilk in an office toilet stall is no longer just degrading—it is illegal. New labour regulations now mandate employers to provide clean, private breastfeeding spaces and dedicated nursing breaks for working mothers. Your livelihood should never come at the expense of your child’s nutrition. This isn’t company benevolence; it is statutory law. If your office hasn’t set up a compliant space, it's time to ask management hard questions.
